prompt:
Image 1 is the camera and pose guide: a grey clay maquette rendered from the game's battle camera, with the pigment in the carved glyphs painted in the god's colour. Copy from it exactly the camera angle, the direction the stone faces, its pose, and its size and place in the frame. Do not copy its smooth clay surfaces, its simplified shapes or the thickness of its limbs: the anatomy, the face and every ornament follow Image 2 and the description.
Image 2 is this god's own approved painted portrait: paint the same stone, with the same shapes, colours, materials and marks, now seen full length from above at the battle camera, in the same painting style. Do not copy its dark background, its candlelight or its framing.

One large painted stone, full length, alone in the image on a perfectly flat, uniform pure green (#00FF00) background, as a game cutout. Pose: standing upright and perfectly still, rooted in its mound.

Camera: high above and in front, looking down at about 40 degrees, the way a player looks down at a miniature on a table; orthographic, with no perspective. The stone's carved front face is toward us and toward the lower left: we see its front face, its left narrow side and its top from above. It is foreshortened as seen from above: its top shows and its height is shortened.

Light: outdoor daylight; the stone stays as dark and as muted as in its portrait, lit only by small warm and cool highlights, never washed out or brightened. A high sun in the upper left of the image lights the top of the stone, the upper surfaces and the upper-left side of the stone with warm highlights; a cool blue-grey sky fill lies in the shadows on the lower-right side. No candlelight, no dramatic dark shadows, nothing glows unless the description below says so. No cast shadow on the background.

Painting style: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, moderate detail, the same hand as the painted portrait; a muted earthy palette with the god's own colours as its portrait shows them, in which the pigment in the carved glyphs in dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour is the one clear hue; soft painterly edges, with small crisp highlights on metal edges and a thin bright rim of light along the upper-left edges of the stone. The stone has a strong, simple, readable silhouette that still reads when it is shrunk to 120 pixels tall. It is not a cartoon: no cel shading, no thick black outlines, no chibi or big-headed proportions, no glossy 3D render, no pixel art.

The god: the Living Monolith, a god that is a single great standing stone: immobile, ancient and aware. Colours: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the stone is the pigment in its carved glyphs: dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Nothing in the image glows: the glyphs are pigment in carved grooves. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.
Body: one tall, rough-hewn slab of grey granite (#7D7A75), about three times as tall as it is wide and a third as thick, its edges weathered and chipped, no capstone: its top is a plain, flat, broken edge; no moss, no vines, no overgrowth; no face, no eyes, no carved features. Glyphs: rows of deeply carved runic glyphs running down both of its broad faces, the grooves filled with a pigment of dull ember-orange (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. Base: its foot is rooted in the ground: it rises from a low mound of dark earth and stones, with thick old roots gripping its base.
The same rows of carved glyphs run down both of its broad faces, the front and the back, so that the colour shows from either side.

Size: the stone fills about 86% of the image along its longest side, placed as in Image 1, with at least 24 pixels of clean background all around; nothing is cropped.

Background: one flat pure green (#00FF00) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor, vignette or shadow. No green anywhere on the figure: no green cloth, no green glow, no green reflections; any lichen grey-green trim stays a pale grey.

Never: text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames, signatures, logos; a floor, ground, scenery or cast shadows; blood; other creatures or people; a cropped figure; smoke, flames, sparks, floating embers or mist.

Image 3 is the finished painted back view of this same monolith on its base (livingMonolith.back.nb21.2k.r2b).

Corrections from the previous attempt, which must be fixed: The base: the same low mound of dark earth, stones and roots as Image 3, seen from the other side.
